notes: The FY2025 20-F lists Ryanair's 93 operating bases (as of May 16, 2025) by airport name only, with no country or per-base aircraft, passenger or staff counts. Counting bases per country would mean mapping airports to countries ourselves, so no country rows were made. Employees by country come from the FY2025 Annual Report's sustainability statement (Table 34, countries with at least 10% of staff: Spain, UK, Italy, Ireland; all others are 'Other', not broken down). No passengers-by-country or taxes-by-country disclosure was found in the 20-F, the Annual Report 2025 or the FY25 Sustainability Report (corporate.ryanair.com); revenue by country (only where above 10%) is already in the records. The Annual Report also says FY25 opened 4 new bases (Dubrovnik, Reggio Calabria, Tangier, Trieste). Sites are 12 of the 'principal facilities owned or leased by the Ryanair Group' table (site area and floor space in square meters, not recorded as values); the same table also lists East Midlands (simulator training), Travel Labs offices in Madrid and Wroclaw, and administrative offices in Warsaw, Pieta (Malta) and Vienna.
